region.text: 'to consolidate the Diyala region, he defeated Sin-abushu, king of Nerebtum'; 'he also annexed Uzarlulu and Tutub'

events.note: c. 1828 BC: Ipiq-Adad II takes the Diyala region. The page: 'massively enlarged his state starting around 1828 BC when he took Arrapha to the north'; 'to consolidate the Diyala region, he defeated Sin-abushu, king of Nerebtum and likely a vassal of Eshnunna'; 'In his campaign against Sin-abushu he also annexed Uzarlulu and Tutub.' Ledger/5 names the Diyala region in its note but resolves only Kirkuk, so the keyframe eshnunna_-1828 snapped 50 Diyala cells in; this event gives them the same year as the Arrapha gain (the Diyala governorate stands in for the district, as in ledger/7).

region.text: Terqa, the Euphrates up river and Tuttul: 'king of Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana'

events.note: c. 1820 BC: Yahdun-Lim's accession; Terqa and the Euphrates to Tuttul are Mari's. The page: reign 'c. 1820 - c. 1797 BC'; he 'started his reign by subduing seven of his rebelling tribal leaders, and rebuilding the walls of Mari and Terqa'; his titles 'king of Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana'; he 'later had to face a rebellion by the Yaminite nomads who were centered at Tuttul'. Terqa is dated by the page to the start of the reign; Tuttul rests on the title (the later rebellion there implies it was his). Moves the dossier's ledger/1 gain (bridged to -1810) to the accession; ledger/1 then changes nothing. Added by the reviewer with keyframe_overrides/1.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria shape plus the eastern margin (see the -2300 keyframe), holding only -2000..-1901: 'The mature phase of the Harappan civilisation lasted from c. 2600-1900 BCE'; from -1900 the Late Harappan shape (keyframe indus-valley-civilization_-1900) applies

keyframe_overrides.why: The page dates the Mature phase '2600-1900 BC' and the Late Harappan (Localisation Era) '1900-1300 BCE' (Punjab/Cemetery H, Jhukar in Sindh, Rangpur in Kachchh, Saurashtra and Gujarat). The dossier's own note says this Mature keyframe holds only -2000..-1901, but with no `to` it stays alive to Cliopatria's row end (-1801) and, unioned with the -1900 Late Harappan keyframe, keeps the full 3,027 cells for -1900..-1801; the dossier's -1900 loss event (1,638 cells) is then undone by a snap. Same correction, explicit years.

correction.text: the Euphrates from Mari through Terqa to Tuttul: "Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana"

keyframe_overrides.why: Yahdun-Lim reigned 'c. 1820 - c. 1797 BC' and 'started his reign by subduing seven of his rebelling tribal leaders, and rebuilding the walls of Mari and Terqa'; his titles were 'king of Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana', and he 'later had to face a rebellion by the Yaminite nomads who were centered at Tuttul'. The page gives Yaggid-Lim (his father) no reign dates or territory, and the dossier's ledger/0 note doubts he even held Mari, so -1830..-1821 is Mari alone (ledger/0). The keyframe, starting -1830, drew Terqa and Tuttul 10 years before Yahdun-Lim's accession (a 53-cell snap); it now starts at his accession, -1820, with the Euphrates gain moved there by events/1. Reviewer 2 Nov 2026: was -1810 (the dossier ledger/1's bridged mid-reign date), which dropped Terqa for the first decade of the reign the page gives it.
